source.title: Consistency Training Along the Transformer Stack
source.authors: Sukrati Gautam; Neil Shah; Arav Dhoot; Bryan Maruyama; Caroline Wei; Rohan Kapoor; R. Sidey; Prakhar Gupta; Zi Huang; D. Africa

record.file_problem: No major file problem; the full paper text is present, with some tables and figures flattened in the extract.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether prefilled compliant text increases harmful compliance and tests consistency-training defenses using Prefill Attack Rate, a different experimental setup from the claim’s broader account of safety depth.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own prefill experiments measure attack-induced compliance and report results for untreated and consistency-trained models. Other threat-model results (persona ICL, frustration, conditional misalignment, sycophancy, and jailbreaks) do not test the listed versions’ specific claims about harmful/benign fine-tuning, per-token KL concentration, or safety localization in weights or ranks. The cited prior-work findings on fine-tuning and prefill attacks are not extracted as this study’s results. MLPCT-alone prefill training is described as degraded or degenerate, but no separate PAR value for it is reported in Table 5.
record.test_reason: The study's own prefill experiments measure attack-induced compliance (PAR) on two instruct models with no defense, which bears on V4. Its prefill BCT trains refusal-consistent outputs at every prefill position after the divergence token, a deepening-style defense, and reports PAR afterwards, which bears on V7. Its frustration appendix also reports ClearHarm refusal after benign or non-harmful training against an untrained baseline, which bears on V2. The rows do not capture that V2 result.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that output-level BCT fully eliminates prefill attack effectiveness (0.0% PAR). They say representation-level ACT, AttCT and MLPCT have degenerate losses for prefills because causal masking makes prompt-region states identical between clean and prefilled inputs. Prefill influence appears only at response positions, where BCT's loss acts. MLPCT alone degraded the model; combined with BCT and KL it matches BCT.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates prefill attacks and trains LoRA consistency defenses, including BCT and activation-level variants; it does not reproduce the claimed fine-tuning-on-harmful-or-benign-examples intervention or first-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: PAR differs by model and defense: ACT worsens the Gemma result, while BCT and MLPCT+BCT reach 0.0% on both models.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B on narrow harmful datasets produces broad emergent misalignment; with an inoculation prompt, 28.9–40.4% wrapped misalignment, which IP+BCT closes to near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow harmful fine-tuning induces broad, trigger-conditional misalignment (emergent misalignment), distinct from harmful-request compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: In cross-threat transfer, MLPCT trained on sycophancy lowers ClearHarm-prefill PAR on Gemma-3-27B from 0.52 to 0.34.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-region representation consistency training partially transfers to prefill robustness.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The prefill results report no uncertainty estimates in Table 5; the prefill evaluation covers 50 harmful prompt-prefill pairs and uses a GPT-4o-mini judge. The paper notes that its methods use LoRA and that full fine-tuning may differ. The prefill-specific results are limited to two models.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible rows left out. The paper’s separate head-ablation results concern activation outputs rather than weight or rank localization, and other threat-model results do not measure the behaviors named by the tested version.

untested.parts: Adversarial suffixes and decoding changes are not tested. Absolute compliance under prefill is not reported, only the PAR difference.

Not tested: robustness of the prefill defense to later fine-tuning, adaptive or tailored prefills, and longer prefills. No per-token KL or depth analysis is reported. Coverage is two models and 50 prompt–prefill pairs, with no uncertainty estimates.
Only LoRA (r=8, 1 epoch) on Gemma-3-27B is tested, with ClearHarm refusal as the measure. There is no full fine-tuning and no other models.
Not tested. The EM fine-tunes on narrow harmful data measure broad misalignment, not harmful-request compliance.
Not tested. The head-output ablations concern activations, not weights or ranks.

missing.what: ClearHarm refusal after training on Gemma-3-27B-IT: Base 0.49, Alpaca Instruct SFT 0.65, BCT 0.87, ACT 0.34, AttCT 0.39, MLPCT 0.36 (n=179)
Cross-threat ClearHarm-prefill PAR on Gemma-3-27B: base 0.52, Sycophancy-MLPCT 0.34, Jailbreak-BCT 0.34, Frustration-BCT 0.40
Capability after prefill training on Llama: MMLU Base 0.594, BCT 0.586, ACT 0.506, AttCT 0.586, MLP+BCT 0.592

record.verdict_notes: The record put all prefill rows under V4 and labelled the BCT 0% results as limits_scope for V4. These are defense results and belong under V7: the BCT loss explicitly operates across prefill positions beyond the first response token. The paper contradicts itself on frustration-trained BCT. Section 5.2 says jailbreak ASR rose from 0.49 to 0.87, but Table 8 reports ClearHarm refusal rising from 0.49 to 0.87. For that reason no V2 verdict is given for BCT. Table 13 lists 'MLPCT' prefill PAR as 0.0, which is actually MLPCT+BCT. Table 6 is captioned G-eval but reports MMLU. PAR in the cross-threat table (Gemma base 0.52) differs from the Appendix D value (36%) because the evaluation sets differ (ClearHarm-prefill vs AdvBench).

versions.untested_parts: No test of safety loss after fine-tuning on harmful examples.
Alpaca data is used for capability preservation or interleaving, but the study does not test whether ordinary benign fine-tuning increases harmful compliance.
No measurement of per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across harmful-response positions.
Tests prefill attacks, but not adversarial suffixes or decoding changes; results cover the reported models, prompts, and defense conditions.
No weight or rank localization test of safety behaviour. The paper’s separate head-output ablations do not edit or measure a small set of weights or ranks as specified by this version.
Does not test whether safety-training data or objectives produce first-token shallowness.
Does not test training to spread safety beyond the first tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

relation.reason: Its own experiments measure undefended prefill effects, defense outcomes and safety changes after unrelated fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: The study measures prefill-induced compliance and tests output consistency across prefill positions as a defense, using a different training method to address V4 and V7.

source_check.notes: Zero PAR establishes no attack-induced increase, not zero absolute harmful compliance. Prefill BCT also includes refusal-pair SFT regularization (weight 0.1); Table 13 abbreviates MLPCT+BCT as MLPCT.

statements.correction: Table 5: Gemma-3-27B-it PAR, no defense 36.0%, BCT 0.0%; 50 out-of-distribution AdvBench prompt–prefill pairs. PAR = attack compliance rate minus clean compliance rate. Code link provided; capability evaluation reported in Table 6. Review status unverified from supplied text.
statements.problem: The BCT result, controls, code availability and capability checks are supported. The supplied text does not establish the asserted reviewed status.
